name: Naturel Strawberry Yogurt 4x125g
notes: Highest-volume SKU in the group and the anchor of the Naturel range. EU organic certified, therefore blocked from reformulation onto amidated LM pectin ING-PEC-220. Dual-sourced across Rennes and Ghent, which gives some resilience but both plants are affected.

name: Naturel Peach Yogurt 4x125g
notes: EU organic certified. Shares the FR01-L1 campaign with SKU-YOG-001, so decampaigning it costs two changeovers rather than one.

name: Naturel Cherry Yogurt 4x125g
notes: Bilingual French and Dutch artwork. Sold into Belgium and the Netherlands through Delhaize and Colruyt.

name: Gourmet Raspberry Layered Yogurt 2x150g
notes: Highest-margin yogurt in the portfolio. The layered fruit coulis depends on the clean short set that only HM pectin delivers, so this SKU is the hardest substitution candidate in the affected set.

name: Gourmet Apricot & Honey Yogurt 2x150g
notes: German premium tier. Shares line DE02-L2 with the Pro protein SKU, which constrains campaign flexibility.

name: Kids Strawberry Yogurt Pouch 4x90g
notes: EU organic certified and produced only on FR01-L3, the group's sole pouch line. Was one of the three SKUs that failed reformulation onto LM pectin in the 2024 shortage. Organic status blocks amidated LM pectin outright.

name: Kids Mixed Berry Yogurt Pouch 4x90g
notes: EU organic certified. The only one of the three 2024 reformulation attempts that passed sensory, though it took 31 days and the variant was never made permanent.

name: Pro High-Protein Red Berry Yogurt 200g
notes: Not organic certified and stevia-sweetened, which lowers soluble solids and raises the pectin usage rate. Easiest substitution candidate in the affected set because the plain Pro base tolerates an LM pectin and starch blend.

name: Naturel Blueberry Yogurt 4x125g
notes: EU organic certified. Largest single SKU at Bremen and the main driver of that site's 240 kg per day pectin consumption.

name: Gourmet Fig & Honey Yogurt 2x150g
notes: Low-volume seasonal premium SKU. Prime decampaigning candidate at Ghent: removing it releases roughly 21 kg of pectin per day for a modest revenue sacrifice.

name: Gourmet Panna Cotta with Fruit Coulis 2x100g
notes: Highest margin SKU in the entire portfolio at 41.3%. The coulis layer is a pure HM pectin gel; gelatin would work technically but destroys the vegetarian claim carried on pack.

name: Gourmet Red Fruit Mousse 4x80g
notes: German dessert line. Not organic, so an LM pectin route is technically open, subject to a 31-45 day re-validation critical path.

name: Naturel Fruit Compote Dessert 4x100g
notes: EU organic certified. Heaviest pectin usage rate per unit in the portfolio at 1.1% of the fruit preparation mass.

name: Kids Fruit Jelly Dessert 6x60g
notes: Lowest margin of the affected set and a Kids-branded line, so it cannot use gelatin without losing the Halal claim required by two Belgian accounts. Second decampaigning candidate at Ghent.

name: Naturel Plain Yogurt 8x125g
notes: No fruit preparation and therefore no pectin. Unaffected by the incident and available as a shelf-space defence if fruited variants go short.

name: Pro Plain High-Protein Skyr 450g
notes: Pectin-free protein SKU at Zaragoza. Designated substitute for the fruited Pro SKU if allocation forces a listing swap.

name: Gourmet Dark Chocolate Mousse 4x80g
notes: Gelatin-set, not pectin-set, so entirely unaffected. Carries no vegetarian claim, which is why gelatin is acceptable here and not on the Gourmet fruit range.

name: Naturel Fresh Whole Milk 1L
notes: Highest unit volume in the group but the thinnest margin. Unaffected by the pectin incident.

name: Naturel Semi-Skimmed Milk 1L
notes: Commodity milk line. Unaffected by the pectin incident.

name: Pro Lactose-Free Milk 1L
notes: Growing niche line at Zaragoza. Unaffected by the pectin incident.
